title: Synthetic fallback validation and operator lab runbook
intro:
Purpose: This runbook describes an operational lab and validation procedure for exercising and verifying the platform's automated fallback behaviors (model variant fallbacks, regional routing fallbacks, and degraded-capacity graceful degradations). The document is intended for Platform Operators, SREs, and on-call engineers running synthetic validation campaigns before and after rollouts that touch routing, capacity, or model-variant policies.

Scope: Applies to Redwood Inference hosted and dedicated deployments. The lab focuses on non-customer traffic synthetic tests that validate: routing decisions, fallback correctness, cache/KV handoff safety, SLI preservation, and alerting fidelity. This runbook does not change production routing policies — it only runs synthetic traffic through established operator tooling and feature-flag sandboxes.
roles_and_ownership:
- Run owner: Platform Reliability Lead (primary contact during the lab)
- Operator in charge: the on-call platform operator who executes the scenario
- Observability owner: Metrics & Dashboards team (maintains dashboards and queries)
- QA verifier: Applied ML & Evals (validates model quality regressions after fallback)
- Escalation contacts: Platform Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime Oncall
preconditions:
- Lab cluster or synthetic namespace present and approved (namespace: synthetic-fallbacks)
- Canary feature-flag toggles available for fallback policies (ff: fallback-lab-enabled)
- Test models and model variants deployed to synthetic namespace (model IDs prefixed with synthetic-)
- Approval from affected service owners for any regional routing tests (email thread or ticket)
- Maintenance window logged if tests may generate alerts visible to customer teams
slo_and_acceptance_criteria:
- Primary SLOs validated in lab (pass/fail criteria):
  1) Routing correctness: 100% of synthetic requests tagged with test-id are routed through the expected fallback path when primary path is intentionally degraded.
  2) Degradation latency cap: 95th-percentile latency under fallback <= 1.5x baseline for synthetic workload.
  3) Token-cost delta: aggregated token cost for fallback path <= 1.4x baseline for same workload.
  4) Alert fidelity: Only lab-specific fallback alerts (labelled synthetic=true) fire; no customer-impacting alerts should trigger.
runbook_steps:
Step 0 — Pre-check (15m)
- Confirm maintenance window and that stakeholders are notified.
- Verify ff: fallback-lab-enabled == false in production. Changes will be made in synthetic namespace only.
- Run quick health checks:
  * kubectl -n synthetic-fallbacks get pods -l app=serving-runtime
  * ./infra/ops/check-kv-cache-health --namespace synthetic-fallbacks

Step 1 — Enable lab and baseline capture (20m)
1. Toggle feature flag for synthetic namespace only:
   * curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
     "https://featureflags.redwood.corp/api/toggles/fallback-lab-enabled" \
     -d '{"namespace":"synthetic-fallbacks","enabled":true}'
2. Start baseline traffic generator (script lives in ops/tools):
   * ./ops/tools/synth-client --namespace synthetic-fallbacks --model synthetic-gpt-medium \
     --qps 10 --duration 10m --tag lab=baseline-$(date +%s)
3. Capture baseline dashboards (note dashboard snapshot IDs):
   * Dashboards: Synthetic Fallbacks — Latency, Token Cost, Routing Paths

Step 2 — Induce primary-path degradation (30m)
- Methods (choose one; prefer non-destructive):
  A) Rate-limited injection: apply an Envoy rate limit to primary pool
     * kubectl -n synthetic-fallbacks apply -f manifests/envoy-rate-limit.yaml
  B) Simulated eviction: soft-evict a serving node from primary pool (use operator CLI)
     * opsctl serving evict --pool primary-synthetic --count 1 --dry-run=false --reason "Fallback lab"
- Validate the chosen degradation is visible to the routing decision logs:
  * kubectl -n synthetic-fallbacks logs -l app=router --tail=200 | grep "route_decision"

Step 3 — Validate fallback activation (20m)
- Watch routing dashboard and verify synthetic requests are routed to fallback variant:
  * Confirm routing metric: routing.fallback.count{lab="<id>"} increases
- Run targeted verification queries (Prometheus/Tempo/Traces):
  * PromQL: sum by (route,variant) (increase(routing_decisions_total{namespace="synthetic-fallbacks",lab="<id>"}[1m]))
  * Trace filter: trace.tags.test_id == "<lab-id>" and trace.tags.fallback == "true"
- Quality check: send 20 sample prompt batches to verify output shape & length unchanged and run evals:
  * ./ops/tools/eval-harness --model synthetic-gpt-medium-fallback --prompt-set labs/fallback-sanity-set.json

Step 4 — Stress & duration test (40m)
- Increase QPS to stress target (e.g., 3x baseline) for 30m: monitor CPU/GPU and KV cache hit rates.
  * ./ops/tools/synth-client --qps 30 --duration 30m --tag lab=stress-$(date +%s)
- Watch for SLI regressions; if 95th-percentile latency > 1.5x baseline, abort and roll back.

Step 5 — Rollback simulation and verification (15m)
- Remove induced degradation and ensure routing converges back to primary within 2 minutes.
  * kubectl -n synthetic-fallbacks delete -f manifests/envoy-rate-limit.yaml
- Verify routing metrics show decline in fallback path and baseline metrics restored.

Step 6 — Cleanup and report (30m)
- Disable feature flag for synthetic namespace.
  * curl -X POST ... fallback-lab-enabled -> false
- Collect artifacts: dashboard snapshots, logs, trace IDs, synthetic client output (S3 path), and evaluation reports.
- Fill lab report template and file an action ticket for any failures.
verification_checklist:
- [ ] routing.fallback.count observed and correlated with induced degradation
- [ ] traces show clear fallback decision attributes and no partial writes to customer KV prefixes
- [ ] 95p latency within acceptance or test aborted with justification
- [ ] token-cost delta measured and within thresholds
- [ ] no production-only alerts fired; any unexpected alerts recorded and ticketed
operator_commands_and_examples:
- Start synthetic client (example):
  ./ops/tools/synth-client --namespace synthetic-fallbacks --model synthetic-gpt-medium \
    --qps 10 --duration 600 --concurrency 4 --tag lab=test-20260308

- Evict a node (example):
  opsctl serving evict --pool primary-synthetic --count 1 --reason "Fallback lab"

- Feature flag toggle (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
    "https://featureflags.redwood.corp/api/toggles/fallback-lab-enabled" \
    -d '{"namespace":"synthetic-fallbacks","enabled":true}'
observability_queries_and_dashboards:
- Key metrics (PromQL samples):
  * Routing fallback count by variant:
    sum by (variant) (increase(routing_decisions_total{namespace="synthetic-fallbacks",lab="<id>"}[5m]))
  * 95th-percentile latency:
    histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{namespace="synthetic-fallbacks"}[5m])) by (le))
  * KV cache hit rate:
    increase(kv_cache_hits_total{namespace="synthetic-fallbacks"}[5m]) / increase(kv_cache_requests_total{namespace="synthetic-fallbacks"}[5m])

- Dashboards used:
  1) Synthetic Fallbacks — Routing & Trace Links
  2) Synthetic Resource Pressure — GPU/CPU/I/O
  3) Token Cost & Accounting — per-lab breakdown
safety_and_abort_criteria:
Abort immediately if any of the following occur:
- Any customer-visible SLO in prod regions degrades (SLO alert triggers with prod labels)
- Resource saturation on shared infra > 80% for CPU/GPU in non-synthetic namespaces
- Unexpected KV prefix writes that include production prefixes
- Unauthorized alerts escalate to PagerDuty with >= P1 severity
post_run_artifacts_and_report:
Required artifacts to attach to lab report ticket:
- Dashboard snapshots (PNG) with timestamped view
- Prometheus query results (CSV) for baseline and test intervals
- Trace IDs (Tempo) for representative fallback traces
- synth-client result archive (S3 link)
- Eval harness results and diff report (JSON)
postmortem_and_action_items_template:
- Summary: High-level description of what was exercised and the outcome.
- Timeline: chronological list of key events with timestamps.
- Root cause / Behavior notes: any deviations from expected fallback logic.
- Action items: assign owner, priority, and ETA. Examples:
  * Fix routing decision metric not tagging lab id — owner: Observability, P1, ETA 1w
  * Adjust fallback concurrency throttle to reduce latency — owner: Serving Runtime, P2, ETA 2w
runbook_review_and_frequency:
- Recommended cadence: quarterly for major routing components or after any routing-related PR to serving runtime.
- Reviewer list on each run: Observability, Serving Runtime, Platform SRE, Applied ML.
appendix:
- Lab namespace naming convention:
  * synthetic-fallbacks-<YYYYMMDD>-<operator>
- Minimal manifest excerpt (Envoy rate limit):
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: ConfigMap
  metadata:
    name: envoy-rate-limit
    namespace: synthetic-fallbacks
  data:
    envoy-ratelimit.yaml: |
      domain: fallback-lab
      descriptors:
        - key: primary-pool
          rate_limit:
            unit: minute
            requests_per_unit: 50

- Contact quick list:
  * Oncall Platform SRE: oncall-platform@redwood.corp
  * Observability Slack: #obs-operators
